notes: The numbers that belong to no single card: setup quantities, the turn's shape, the one standing economy rate and the end-game trigger. Anything PRINTED on a card lives in cards.json instead, anything printed on the island lives in island.json, and the five door actions live in workers.json.

SCHEMA VERSION 2 IS v31 (Dean, 02/09/2026, docs/design-changes-v31-2026-09-02-v1.md). The bump is not cosmetic: the file lost seven keys in one edit and every one of them was a coin. If you are reading a v31 number against a report written before 02/09/2026, stop - the reference was re-cut as reference-v10 and no historical number in reports/ is comparable.

THERE ARE NO COINS. Not zero coins: no coin. Nothing is earned in them, nothing is priced in them, there is no coin tie-break and there is no coin knob. What went with the currency, in one list so nobody re-derives it from an old doc: startingCoins, upgradeCostCoins (there are no starter upgrades at all now), coinPityDivisor, visitPayout in all four of its branches, giftDiscardCoins, buyCost (the card buy) and marketCost (buy at market). Six of those seven were already null or already deleted in spirit by 19/08/2026; the seventh, the upgrade price, went with the upgraded faces. The design reason is the standing finding the market note used to carry, taken all the way: money is what buys SOLITAIRE in this game, because a visit is bought with a card and every other bonus option was bought with a coin, so a coin sink in the bonus slot crowds the visit out all game. Deleting the currency deletes the competitor. The 30 Power and Endgame cards now cost 2 cards of their OWN suit, and card text that read GBP 2 or GBP 1 reads Draw 1.

THE TURN, in the order it is played (v31): (1) spend any number of MEEPLES from your supply, one at a time, each performing its colour's plain action and then leaving the game for good; (2) ONE bonus option - Draw 1, or place 1 card from your hand on any Notice Board and immediately perform that board's suit action; (3) ONE core action - Draw, Build, Grow, Harvest, Deliver. Steps 1 and 2 are both start-of-turn. A meeple cannot be held back and spent later in the turn, which is the only thing stopping the meeple supply from being a hand of free actions played reactively.

baseDraw IS 2 SEE, 2 KEEP - the plain Draw action keeps BOTH cards and discards nothing. It was 2-see-1-keep from v13 until v31. The reason for the change is not generosity, it is that the discard was the last piece of hidden bookkeeping in the core five actions and it bought nothing measurable; the game's clock is now the card supply and the end trigger, not a per-draw tax. NOTE THE INTERACTION with bonusDraw below: the plain action and the free bonus option are now the same verb at different sizes, so a seat that takes Draw as its action and Draw 1 as its bonus nets 3 cards a turn with no interaction at all. That is the shape action inflation will show up in first.

THE HAND LIMIT IS BACK, AT A FLAT 12, AND IT IS A GAME RULE RATHER THAN A CARD VALUE (Dean, 02/09/2026, reversing one v31 change on evidence). WHAT THE DELETION MEASURED, because this is the number that decided it: v31 removed the limit and the first simulator run after it found the deletion had quietly removed the bound on the LEGAL-MOVE ENUMERATOR as well. The comment over `subsets` in packages/engine/src/actions.ts read 'hands are 6-8', and that bound WAS the hand limit - nothing else in the game was holding it. With hands reaching 34 cards a 2-seat position offered 43,879 legal moves, 43,845 of them build payments, because C(33,4) is 40,920 ways to pay for ONE buildable card; a re-measurement on 02/09/2026 at n=4 games found a worse position still at 116,535. A 2-seat game went from about 0.1 seconds to 1-15 minutes, so the watch-list suite could only be run at n=8 and every conclusion from that run is an anecdote. The bots hoarded to a median hand of 18, the free bonus Draw 1 became strictly dominant (beating a neighbour visit 3:1, failing the hook assertion) and the 2-seat game ran to 45 rounds. IT IS A DESIGN FAILURE BEFORE IT IS AN ENGINEERING ONE: a gateway player choosing between forty thousand ways to pay for one build is not a shippable turn, and diminishing returns on a card in hand are what make a neighbour worth visiting at all. THE SHAPE OF THE RESTORED RULE IS NOT THE OLD ONE. It is ONE GLOBAL NUMBER, not five printed per-suit ones - the Barn still prints nothing and stays blank, because this belongs on the player aid where a rule that applies to everybody belongs. It is checked at the END of your turn only; you may exceed it mid-turn, which is how several cards work (O14 sows a whole hand, W10 empties one into the barn) and is the old rule kept deliberately. Overflow discards down to the limit at the turn boundary. 12 IS A GUESS AND A KNOB: it is roughly three turns of accumulation above the 4-card opening hand, generous enough that the limit is a brake rather than a clock, and overlays/hand-limit-10.overlay.json and overlays/hand-limit-15.overlay.json are the paired arms, and overlays/hand-limit.sweep.json is the full ladder. null disables the rule and restores the v31 behaviour, which is the control arm nobody should run without reading the numbers above first.

bonusDraw IS THE SOLITAIRE HALF OF THE BONUS SLOT: 1 free card off the top of any one deck in play, taken instead of visiting a Notice Board. It exists so the bonus slot is never dead - a seat with an empty hand has no card to place on a board and would otherwise skip the slot entirely - and it is the yardstick every door has to beat. THAT YARDSTICK IS WHY THE ORCHARD DOOR IS DRAW 3 AND NOT DRAW 2 (see workers.json): a door that hands back 2 cards for the 1 card you place on it is worth exactly the free option, and a rule worth exactly its own alternative is a rule nobody takes. Raising this number is the cheapest way to kill every door in the game at once.

selfVisitAllowed IS RISK 2 OF THE WHOLE PASS, ARMED ON PURPOSE (Dean, 02/09/2026). You may place your bonus card on your OWN Notice Board and take your own suit's action. Every previous version of this game has had the solitaire option crowd the visit out when the two competed for one slot, and this is exactly that shape again, now bought with the same currency as the interaction rather than a cheaper one. Its ONLY brake is structural: your card counts toward your own board's threshold of 2 exactly as a rival's does, so feeding your own board clogs it in two turns, shuts your own door, and locks every neighbour out of your suit's action until you spend a Harvest clearing it. Whether that brake is enough is the single most important thing the first simulator run has to answer. a08-the-hook must count self-visits SEPARATELY and must never credit one as interaction; an assertion that pools them will report a healthy hook while the table plays solitaire. Setting this false is the paired control and restores the v30 rule that a visit is always somebody else's board.

bonusTiming (Dean, 03/09/2026 - A CORRECTION, NOT AN EXPERIMENT): the turn is meeples, then your CORE ACTION, then the bonus option. This engine and both design docs had carried the opposite order since 19/08/2026 ('start': bonus before the action) and were simply wrong about the game. 'start' survives as the paired control (overlays/bonus-first.overlay.json) and 'any' as v14's once-per-turn-any-point (overlays/bonus-any-time.overlay.json). THE THREE ARE NOT ORDERABLE BY POWER: under 'start' a door can fuel the action that follows it, under 'end' the action can set the door up - fill a building then Harvest it through the Wheat door, harvest into the barn then Deliver through the Vegetable one - so expect the DOOR MIX to move and not only the visit rate. SLOT UNSPENT still reads the window, but its absolute is the rational floor and only the delta between arms means anything.

visitCurrency IS THE MEEPLE-LOOP ARM AND IT DEFAULTS TO 'card', WHICH IS THE SHIPPED v31 GAME (Dean, 04/09/2026, docs/meeple-loop-visit-handoff-2026-09-04-v1.md). 'card' is every rule described above this line: a visit costs one card from your hand, the card lands on a Notice Board, the board is a building with a threshold, self-visiting is legal and the bonus slot's other half is a free Draw 1. 'meeple' replaces the whole of that with the meeple loop: a visit costs a MEEPLE placed in the colour slot of a NEIGHBOUR's Notice Board (never your own), the board is not a building at all, and the bonus slot's other half is COLLECT - take every meeple off your own board and Draw 1. IT IS A PAIRED ARM AND NOT A REPLACEMENT: the shipped game has to stay bit-reproducible as the control so that every number the arm produces reads as a delta on identical seeds, which is why this is one knob and not a rewrite. WHAT 'meeple' IGNORES: selfVisitAllowed (there is no self-visit under any flag, ruled X5) and economy.noticeBoardThreshold (the board has no threshold). bonusTiming, bonusSlotsPerTurn and handLimit all still apply and are deliberately unchanged. WHY IT EXISTS: the v31 hook fails because the visit is CONDITIONAL and the free Draw 1 is not, and because being visited pays the host nothing. Measured on reference-v11 seeds at n=1580, the shipped game reads a rival visit on 40.4% of turns against Draw 1 on 67.8%, hook 0.41 against a floor of 0.5. This arm attacks availability and the host side at once, and removes the card from the visit entirely.

startingMeeplesPerColour AND meepleCapPerColour ARE THE ARM'S TWO ECONOMY NUMBERS, and both are read ONLY under visitCurrency 'meeple' (rules R3 and R4). Every player starts with ONE meeple of each of the five colours, NOT drawn from the island bag, so the loop is primed before anybody delivers - a first-turn visit is possible at every seat. The cap says you may never HOLD more than one meeple of a colour: a meeple you would gain of a colour you already hold is returned to the box, whether it came from collecting your own board or from an island delivery, and the engine emits meepleBoxed rather than meepleGained when that happens. THE CAP IS THE ANSWER TO PILES: meeples now recirculate (a spent one moves to the neighbour's board rather than leaving the game), so without a ceiling a seat could sit on a wall of stored actions. Sweep the cap at 1 against 2 and the start at 1 against 0; measure median supply held in the last third, and boxed per game, before touching either.

SETUP IS FOUR CARDS AND NOTHING ELSE. startingHand is 4 from your own suit deck, startingBarnCards is 0, and there are no coins to start with. The barn starts EMPTY, which is new: it used to be seeded with 1 card. The barn is now purely a place to store cards ready for delivery and PRINTS NOTHING - and that survives the hand limit coming back, because the limit is no longer a card value. See turn.handLimit below.

noticeBoardThreshold IS THE ONE ECONOMY NUMBER LEFT, AND IT IS THE BALANCE LEVER. 2 cards and the board clogs; the owner clears it with a Harvest into their own barn. It is the only lever ever measured to move the suit balance, and it was monotone and self-consistent across three paired n=1580 arms on the older two-building surface: at t=4 Orchard won 80.8%, at t=3 62.8%, at t=2 42.0% against an even share of 36.4%. On the later single-door surface at n=500: t=5 clogged 2.3% of turn boundaries (no brake at all), t=3 5%, t=2 11%, with the suit spread most even at 2. Dean's reading of why a loose door is worse than it looks: 'you get to use other players' cards a lot, but that number also decreases how often you can harvest and make use of the cards people give you, making it more valuable to the visitor rather than the person who is visited.' In v31 it throttles a THIRD kind of traffic as well - your own self-visits - so the same 2 is now doing more work than any arm has measured it doing. Never raise it without re-running the suite. null hands the number back to whatever the Notice Board prints; the v31 sheet prints 2, so the long-standing 5-versus-2 drift between this override and the card is CLOSED and this key is now an override that agrees with the print.

endGame.trigger is deliveryCount (Dean, 2026-08-09, with the flat island) and survives v31 untouched in its wording and at risk in its number. The game ends when any ONE seat completes its deliveriesToTrigger-th ISLAND delivery, after which every other player takes furtherTurnsEach more turns. Balloon moves are Deliver actions but not island deliveries, so they never count. It is still one observable trigger read off public state - a receipt count in front of a player - and still a thing a player does rather than a deck running out. It is FLAT at every seat count, so 6 is half the 2-seat island's 12 delivery spaces, a third of the 3-seat island's 18 and a quarter of the 4-seat island's 24; that asymmetry is known and taken, and 2p is where to watch it. WHY IT IS NOW THE FIRST KNOB TO SWEEP: v31's bonus slot buys a FULL CORE ACTION for one card (the Wheat door is a free Harvest, the Dairy door a free Build) and meeples add uncapped free actions on top, so turns are materially more powerful than v30's and the same 6 deliveries arrive sooner. Expect a shorter game and higher scores before anything is dialled. overlays/end-trigger-8.overlay.json is the paired arm; overlays/end-trigger.sweep.json is the full ladder.
unresolved: ACTION INFLATION (risk 1, v31). The bonus slot now buys a whole core action for one card and the meeple supply adds free ones with no cap, so actions resolved per turn is the number this entire pass moves and nothing in the suite currently measures it. It has to be measured BEFORE deliveriesToTrigger is dialled, or the dial will be set against an unknown.

THE HOOK, under self-visiting (risk 2). Open until a08-the-hook reports visit-a-neighbour and visit-yourself as two separate lines and the neighbour line holds up. If the self-visit share climbs while the neighbour share falls, the fix is not a new rule: it is selfVisitAllowed false, or the clog brake being made sharper.

THE MONOCULTURE PULL (risk 3). The Farmstead pays 1 VP per own-suit card built and the Power and Endgame cards cost 2 cards of their own suit. Both push the same way, and the Innovation lens's standing constraint is that the metric axis must not be the specialisation axis. The own-crop build share was 82.6% before this change; it can only go up. Watch it, and note that neither of the two pulls is a knob - undoing either is a card change.

THE APIARY DOOR IS THE WEAKEST ON THE TABLE AND WAS RULED THAT WAY KNOWINGLY (Dean, 02/09/2026). Sow 1 FROM YOUR HAND means a visitor pays 2 cards for 1 threshold step, which is the self-cancellation problem in its purest form. Measure the door mix; if the Apiary board takes no traffic, the fix is to move the sown card back to a deck top, not to make the door cheaper.

The 2-seat game is still the seat count with the least evidence behind it. deliveriesToTrigger is flat, the island is half-used at 12 spaces, and a clogged Notice Board at 2 players is total denial rather than a race. Nothing here is wrong on paper; it has simply never been played.
